prompt: Public-to-private buyers often pay a control premium over the unaffected share price because:

options.text: Minority passive stakes trade at the same price as full control
Public shareholders require no premium when delisting
Control premiums apply only to distressed companies
They acquire 100% ownership and can change strategy, capital structure, and synergies

explanation: Control value reflects full decision rights and integration benefits unavailable to minority public holders.

distractorExplanations.b: Delisting full companies typically requires premium to induce tender.
distractorExplanations.c: Control premium is not limited to distress.

prompt: Sensitivity tables in investment banking pitch books commonly vary:

options.text: WACC and terminal growth, or exit multiples and leverage in LBO contexts
Only the font size of the chart title
Historical stock split ratios from decades ago
The CEO's age and tenure

explanation: Sensitivities show valuation range under key assumption changes investors care about.

distractorExplanations.c: Old splits do not drive DCF ranges.
distractorExplanations.d: Management bio is not a valuation variable.

prompt: An equity value bridge from enterprise value typically subtracts:

options.text: Only revenue with no balance sheet items
Net debt, preferred stock, minority interest, and other non-common claims as applicable
Future capex budgets with no debt adjustment
Marketing expenses from the income statement

explanation: EV to equity bridge removes all claims ahead of common shareholders.

distractorExplanations.a: Revenue alone does not bridge EV to equity.
distractorExplanations.c: Capex budgets are not the standard bridge line.
distractorExplanations.d: Operating expenses are not subtracted from EV for equity value.

prompt: EV/Revenue multiples are often used instead of EV/EBITDA when:

options.text: Every mature industrial company prefers revenue multiples
Debt balances are zero by definition
The company is unprofitable or EBITDA is negative or not meaningful
Tax rates exceed 100%

explanation: Revenue can benchmark high-growth or pre-profit firms where EBITDA multiples distort comparisons.

distractorExplanations.a: Profitable mature firms often use EBITDA or earnings multiples.
distractorExplanations.b: Debt level does not dictate multiple choice.
distractorExplanations.d: Tax rates do not determine multiple selection that way.

prompt: Mid-year convention in a DCF adjusts discount periods because:

options.text: All cash is received on December 31
Discount rates must be doubled
Terminal value is excluded from the model
Cash flows are assumed to arrive evenly through the year, not all at year-end

explanation: Mid-year discounting (e.g., t − 0.5) avoids overstating the present value of annual flows.

distractorExplanations.a: Year-end convention assumes end-of-year receipt; mid-year differs.
distractorExplanations.b: Discount rates are not doubled for convention.
distractorExplanations.c: Terminal value remains part of DCF.

prompt: Circular reference in an LBO model (interest expense affecting debt paydown) is typically resolved by:

options.text: Enabling iterative calculation or a circularity switch in the spreadsheet until balances converge
Deleting all debt from the capital structure
Setting interest expense to zero permanently
Using only book value with no cash flow forecast

explanation: Interest depends on debt balance; debt paydown depends on cash available after interest—iteration solves the loop.

distractorExplanations.b: Removing debt avoids LBO mechanics entirely.
distractorExplanations.d: Book value alone does not model LBO returns.

prompt: Under ASC 842 operating leases, enterprise value analysis may need to:

options.text: Ignore all lease commitments because they are off-balance-sheet with no effect
Treat capitalized operating lease obligations similarly to debt when comparing levered profiles across companies
Add lease expense to revenue without adjustment
Remove all depreciation because leases replaced it entirely

explanation: Capitalized lease liabilities affect net debt and comparability; analysts often add lease-adjusted debt to EV bridges.

distractorExplanations.a: ASC 842 brought many leases on balance sheet; they matter for leverage.
distractorExplanations.c: Lease expense adjustment is not simply added to revenue.
distractorExplanations.d: Depreciation treatment is separate from lease capitalization.

prompt: A non-binding letter of intent in M&A usually outlines:

options.text: Final binding purchase price with no further negotiation permitted
Guaranteed regulatory approval in all jurisdictions
Immediate closing without confirmatory due diligence
Indicative price, structure, diligence timeline, and exclusivity terms subject to definitive agreements

explanation: LOIs set expectations and process terms but definitive docs and diligence determine final deal.

distractorExplanations.a: LOIs are typically non-binding on price until final docs.
distractorExplanations.b: Regulatory approval is never guaranteed in an LOI.
distractorExplanations.c: Confirmatory diligence follows LOI in most processes.

prompt: An exclusivity (no-shop) clause during sell-side negotiations generally allows the seller to:

options.text: Negotiate only with the designated buyer for a defined period, with limited fiduciary out for superior proposals
Solicit unlimited competing bids publicly during the entire period without exception
Terminate the deal without any break-up fee in every case
Share confidential data with unlimited third parties freely

explanation: Exclusivity focuses the process on one buyer while preserving board fiduciary duties in material respects.

distractorExplanations.c: Break-up fees may still apply per contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Data sharing is restricted under confidentiality.

prompt: Accretion/dilution analysis in a stock merger compares:

options.text: Only the target's historical book value per share
Pro forma combined EPS to the acquirer's standalone EPS
Combined revenue to the acquirer's headcount
Target EBITDA to acquirer cash balance

explanation: Stock deals are screened for whether the exchange ratio increases or decreases acquirer EPS.

distractorExplanations.a: Book value alone is not accretion/dilution focus.
distractorExplanations.d: Cash balance does not define EPS accretion.

prompt: A hostile takeover bid may be launched through:

options.text: A friendly board-approved merger agreement
An informal phone call to one employee
A tender offer directly to shareholders without board approval of the transaction
Voluntary delisting without shareholder vote

explanation: Unsolicited tender offers bypass target management when the board resists negotiation.

distractorExplanations.b: Informal calls are not a takeover mechanism.
distractorExplanations.d: Delisting requires corporate action and votes.

prompt: Management presentations in a sell-side auction are typically delivered to:

options.text: The general public through open webcast without NDA
Only the target company's rank-and-file employees
Regulators before any buyer is identified
Qualified prospective bidders after signing confidentiality agreements

explanation: CIM and management meetings follow NDAs to protect sensitive financial and strategic information.

distractorExplanations.a: Public disclosure precedes regulated marketing in registered offerings, not private auctions.
distractorExplanations.b: Employee-only meetings are not the buyer process.
distractorExplanations.c: Regulator-first presentation is not standard sell-side order.

prompt: A collar in a stock-for-stock merger protects against:

options.text: Exchange ratio fluctuation if the acquirer's or target's share price moves beyond agreed bands
All regulatory risk including HSR clearance automatically
Every post-closing integration cost without limit
Currency translation on foreign subsidiaries

explanation: Collars fix or float the ratio within limits so neither party bears unlimited price movement before close.

distractorExplanations.c: Integration costs are not collar mechanics.
distractorExplanations.d: Collars address share price, not FX of subs alone.

prompt: Representation and warranty insurance in M&A primarily shifts:

options.text: All antitrust liability to the target's customers
Breach risk from seller indemnities toward an insurer, often reducing escrow holdbacks
Tax filing obligations to employees
D&O liability for directors to retail shareholders automatically

explanation: RWI lets buyers pursue claims against insurers for covered reps instead of solely chasing seller escrows.

distractorExplanations.a: Antitrust remains with parties and regulators.
distractorExplanations.c: Tax obligations stay with the entity and buyers.
distractorExplanations.d: D&O coverage is a separate policy type.

prompt: A locked-box mechanism sets purchase price based on:

options.text: Future EBITDA achieved only after closing without adjustment
Random lottery among shareholders
Equity value at a historical balance sheet date, with cash generated after that date accruing to the buyer (subject to leakage covenants)
Daily stock price averaging after closing indefinitely

explanation: Locked-box fixes price at a reference date; economic benefit from that date belongs to the buyer, and leakage covenants stop the seller from extracting value.

distractorExplanations.a: Post-close EBITDA earnouts differ from locked-box.
distractorExplanations.b: Price is not set by lottery.
distractorExplanations.d: Post-close averaging is not locked-box mechanics.

prompt: A go-shop provision in a merger agreement allows the target to:

options.text: Never contact any other bidder under any circumstance
Immediately break the deal with zero fees
Sell assets to competitors without board approval freely
Solicit alternative proposals for a limited period after signing the initial agreement

explanation: Go-shops test the market briefly after a signed deal to confirm no superior offer exists.

distractorExplanations.c: Asset sales require governance and covenants.

prompt: Strategic acquirers differ from financial sponsors in that strategics often pursue:

options.text: Operating synergies, portfolio fit, and integration with existing business lines
Only dividend recapitalizations with no operating involvement
Mandatory liquidation of the target within 30 days
Exclusive focus on short-term trading gains without holding assets

explanation: Strategics buy for commercial rationale; sponsors seek financial returns via leverage and eventual exit.

distractorExplanations.b: Recaps are sponsor tools, not defining strategic motive.
distractorExplanations.c: Liquidation is not a typical strategic goal.
distractorExplanations.d: Sponsors hold for value creation, not day trading.

prompt: A Hart-Scott-Rodino second request typically:

options.text: Eliminates all U.S. filing requirements permanently
Extends antitrust review by requiring substantial additional documents and information
Guarantees immediate clearance within one business day
Applies only to private companies with zero revenue

explanation: Second requests pause the waiting period until agencies complete deeper competitive analysis.

distractorExplanations.a: HSR obligations remain until terminated or expired.
distractorExplanations.c: Second requests lengthen review, not shorten it.
distractorExplanations.d: Size-of-person thresholds can capture private firms.

prompt: Virtual data rooms in sell-side M&A control access by:

options.text: Publishing all files on an unsecured public website
Allowing unlimited download without audit trail
Granting permissioned logins, watermarking documents, and tracking user activity
Sharing passwords company-wide on social media

explanation: VDRs protect confidentiality and provide diligence evidence through access controls and logging.

distractorExplanations.d: Public password sharing breaches process integrity.

prompt: A dual-track process in restructuring or sale means:

options.text: Running two unrelated IPOs simultaneously in different countries
Merging two buyers into one legal entity before bidding
Issuing dual-class stock without shareholder vote
Pursuing an out-of-court sale or restructuring alongside Chapter 11 preparation

explanation: Dual-track preserves optionality between negotiated sale and bankruptcy if a deal is not reached.

distractorExplanations.a: Dual IPO is not the M&A meaning.
distractorExplanations.c: Dual-class shares are capital structure, not process.

prompt: A forward triangular merger structure is often used to:

options.text: Acquire the target through a subsidiary merger while keeping the parent as the surviving public entity
Liquidate the acquirer and dissolve the target automatically
Avoid all shareholder votes in every jurisdiction without exception
Convert all debt to equity without documentation

explanation: Forward triangles merge target into acquirer sub; parent remains and often avoids direct asset transfer complexity.

distractorExplanations.c: Shareholder votes may still be required.
distractorExplanations.d: Debt conversion requires contractual or bankruptcy process.

prompt: Poison pills and staggered boards primarily affect hostile bids by:

options.text: Guaranteeing any bidder immediate 100% ownership at book value
Diluting or delaying acquirer ability to gain control without board negotiation
Eliminating all fiduciary duties of the target board
Forcing automatic sale to the first bidder regardless of price

explanation: Shareholder rights plans and classified boards raise cost and time for unsolicited control attempts.

distractorExplanations.a: Pills deter rapid control; they do not grant cheap control.
distractorExplanations.d: Boards can reject inadequate offers.

prompt: A confidential information memorandum in sell-side M&A is distributed to:

options.text: Retail investors through a free public website without registration
All employees before any buyer qualification
Media outlets under embargo without buyer status
Potential buyers who have signed confidentiality agreements after initial screening

explanation: CIMs contain non-public financial and operational detail for qualified bidders only.

distractorExplanations.a: Public retail distribution would violate securities laws for private M&A.
distractorExplanations.b: Broad employee distribution is not the marketing path.
distractorExplanations.c: Press does not replace qualified buyer process.

prompt: An accelerated bookbuild for a follow-on equity offering means:

options.text: Marketing and pricing occur in a compressed window, often overnight, to reduce market risk
The issuer waits six months between order collection and pricing
Only bonds may be sold, never equity
Retail brokers set the final price without underwriter input

explanation: ABBs quickly gather institutional demand and set final price/volume in days or hours.

distractorExplanations.c: Bookbuilds apply to equity and sometimes convertibles.
distractorExplanations.d: Underwriters lead pricing in firm/ best-efforts contexts.

prompt: A 144A-for-life high-yield bond is sold:

options.text: Only to individuals in registered public offerings on Form S-1
To qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A without a subsequent SEC registration for resale
Exclusively on municipal tax-exempt platforms
Without any disclosure document to any investor

explanation: 144A-for-life relies on QIB private placement exemptions for both issuance and trading restrictions.

distractorExplanations.a: Registered public retail offerings use different rules.
distractorExplanations.c: Municipal tax-exempt is a separate market.
distractorExplanations.d: Offering memoranda still provide disclosure.

prompt: An at-the-market (ATM) equity program lets an issuer:

options.text: Conduct only a single fixed-price tender to insiders
Borrow unlimited cash from the Fed discount window
Sell shares into the open market at prevailing prices through a sales agent over time
Repurchase all outstanding shares in one day without disclosure

explanation: ATMs dribble out primary shares opportunistically with lower market impact than block deals.

distractorExplanations.a: Tenders differ from ATM dribble sales.
distractorExplanations.b: Fed discount window is banking, not equity ATM.
distractorExplanations.d: Large repurchases require authorization and disclosure.

prompt: In a best-efforts underwriting, the underwriter:

options.text: Must purchase all unsold securities from the issuer at the offer price
Guarantees the issuer's stock price after listing
Acts as issuer's legal counsel on tax matters
Uses commercially reasonable efforts to sell securities but does not commit to buy unsold shares

explanation: Best efforts shift unsold risk to the issuer; firm commitment underwriters buy the offering.

distractorExplanations.a: Buying unsold shares describes firm commitment.
distractorExplanations.b: Price guarantees are not underwriting terms.

prompt: IPO lock-up agreements typically restrict:

options.text: Company insiders and major shareholders from selling shares for a period after the offering
The underwriter from publishing a prospectus
The SEC from reviewing the registration statement
Retail investors from buying shares in the aftermarket

explanation: Lock-ups reduce post-IPO supply pressure from pre-IPO holders and align with stabilization period.

distractorExplanations.c: SEC review is not restricted by lock-up.
distractorExplanations.d: Retail may trade freely after listing.

prompt: A dual-tranche bond offering might include:

options.text: Only common stock and warrants with no debt component
Senior secured notes alongside senior unsecured notes with different collateral packages and yields
Municipal general obligation bonds for corporate issuers
Physical commodities instead of securities

explanation: Issuers split credit risk tiers to broaden investor demand and optimize pricing.

distractorExplanations.a: Equity-only is not a bond dual-tranche.
distractorExplanations.c: Corporate issuers do not issue munis.
distractorExplanations.d: Commodity tranches are not standard bond structures.

prompt: Green bond issuers commit to allocate proceeds toward:

options.text: Unrestricted general corporate purposes with no project linkage
Only executive compensation increases
Eligible environmental projects tracked and often reported to investors
Cryptocurrency mining without disclosure

explanation: Green-labeled bonds tie use of proceeds to climate or environmental projects per framework (e.g., ICMA principles).

distractorExplanations.b: Executive pay is not green use of proceeds.
distractorExplanations.d: Undisclosed crypto use would violate green bond norms.

prompt: Rule 10b5-1 trading plans allow insiders to:

options.text: Trade on material nonpublic information whenever convenient
Avoid all Section 16 reporting obligations
Sell unlimited shares without any plan documentation
Pre-schedule trades under a written plan adopted in good faith when not in possession of MNPI

explanation: Affirmative defense plans set automatic sales/purchases to reduce appearance of trading on MNPI.

distractorExplanations.b: Section 16 still applies to reporting insiders.

prompt: An incurrence covenant in bond indentures typically allows additional debt only if:

options.text: Pro forma financial tests (e.g., leverage or coverage ratios) are satisfied
The issuer wishes to borrow with no limits or tests
Any competitor approves the new borrowing
Stock price falls below $1 per share automatically

explanation: Incurrence tests gate new debt on credit metrics; maintenance covenants require ongoing compliance.

distractorExplanations.d: Stock price alone is not standard incurrence test.

prompt: An equity carve-out IPO involves:

options.text: Dissolving the parent and merging all subs simultaneously
Selling a minority stake in a subsidiary while the parent retains control
Selling 100% of the parent with no subsidiary retained
Converting all subsidiary debt to perpetual preferred automatically

explanation: Carve-outs monetize a division and establish public currency while parent keeps majority ownership.

distractorExplanations.a: Parent dissolution is not a carve-out.
distractorExplanations.c: 100% parent sale is not minority carve-out.
distractorExplanations.d: Automatic debt conversion is not carve-out definition.

prompt: Fintech issuer Northloop plans a $25 million raise, to be advertised on LinkedIn and its website, and will sell to accredited investors exclusively. Which offering exemption fits?

options.text: Rule 506(b), since every buyer will be accredited
Rule 506(c), verifying each buyer's accredited status
Regulation Crowdfunding, as it permits online advertising
Rule 504, which lets issuers advertise in any state

explanation: The general-solicitation track of Rule 506 permits public online ads if every purchaser is accredited and the issuer takes reasonable steps to verify that status, not just a self-certification. Rule 506 has no dollar cap, so a $25 million raise fits.

distractorExplanations.c: Regulation Crowdfunding caps raises at $5 million in 12 months and must run through a registered portal, far below $25 million.
distractorExplanations.d: Rule 504 caps offerings at $10 million in 12 months and allows general solicitation only under qualifying state registration.

prompt: Liability management exercises (e.g., debt tender offers) often aim to:

options.text: Increase principal owed without holder approval in every case

Eliminate SEC reporting for public issuers permanently
Refinance or extend maturities, reduce coupons, or amend covenants with holder consent

explanation: LM transactions restructure outstanding bonds when issuers seek lower cost or flexibility.

distractorExplanations.b: Forced equity conversion requires exchange offers.
distractorExplanations.c: Reporting obligations persist for public issuers.

prompt: Stapled financing offered by a sell-side advisor provides:

options.text: Pre-arranged debt commitment letters bidders can use to fund the acquisition
Free legal opinions to all employees of the target
Guaranteed antitrust approval from DOJ
Permanent elimination of all financing condition in every bid

distractorExplanations.d: Financing conditions may remain in bids.

prompt: Reverse inquiry in a bond new-issue process refers to:

Mandatory retail order period on Form S-1 equity
Rating agency downgrade during roadshow

explanation: Reverse inquiry helps bankers gauge demand and structure for opportunistic or window offerings.

distractorExplanations.c: Retail order periods relate to registered equity.
distractorExplanations.d: Downgrades are credit events, not reverse inquiry.

prompt: FINRA's Series 79 examination qualifies registered persons to participate in:

options.text: Retail mutual fund sales without any supervisory principal
Real estate brokerage licensing nationwide
Medical malpractice litigation
Investment banking representative activities such as M&A, underwriting, and restructuring

explanation: Series 79 is the IB representative exam covering primary and advisory IB functions under FINRA rules.

distractorExplanations.a: Retail fund sales use other exams (e.g., S6/S7 paths).
distractorExplanations.c: Legal malpractice is outside securities licensing.

prompt: SEC Regulation S-K Item 402 requires disclosure of:

options.text: Executive compensation including summary comp tables and related policies
Only the company's water utility bills
Personal social media posts of all interns
Daily trading volume of unrelated ETFs

explanation: Item 402 governs named executive officer pay disclosure in public company filings.

distractorExplanations.b: Utility bills are immaterial operating detail.
distractorExplanations.c: Intern social media is not Item 402.
distractorExplanations.d: Unrelated ETF volume is not issuer compensation disclosure.

options.text: All securities sales regardless of investor count without limit since 1933
Transactions not involving a public offering (private placements)
Only municipal bond offerings to foreign governments
Registered Form S-1 initial public offerings

prompt: A shelf takedown under Rule 415 often uses:

options.text: No filing because shelves require zero SEC documents
Only oral statements with no written supplement
A prospectus supplement updating the base shelf registration for the specific issuance
Blue sky registration in one state only with no federal filing

prompt: FINRA Rule 5130 restricts:

options.text: All retail investors from ever buying IPO stock
Issuers from hiring underwriters
The SEC from reviewing registration statements
Sharing in IPO allocations with certain covered persons (e.g., brokers' restricted persons)

explanation: 5130 (new issues) limits IPO flipping and allocation to industry insiders and related accounts.

prompt: Rule 144 resale holding period for affiliates of reporting issuers is generally:

options.text: Six months if the company has been subject to Exchange Act reporting for at least 90 days
One business day for all securities without condition
Ten years for every private placement regardless of status
Zero days with no restrictions for all affiliates

distractorExplanations.c: Ten years is not the standard Rule 144 period.
distractorExplanations.d: Affiliates face conditions, not zero restrictions.

prompt: Regulation Crowdfunding (Reg CF) caps the amount an issuer may raise in a 12-month period at approximately:

options.text: $50 billion with no investor limits
$5 million (as amended under current SEC rules)
$1,000 total for all issuers combined nationally
Unlimited if the issuer is private with zero disclosure

prompt: Exchange Act Rule 10b-5 prohibits:

options.text: Only physical theft of stock certificates from vaults
Lawful disclosure under Regulation FD
Fraud in connection with the purchase or sale of securities, including material misstatements and omissions
All trading during regular market hours

explanation: 10b-5 is the principal antifraud rule enforced by SEC and used in insider trading cases.

Exempt follow-on offerings from prospectus delivery

Only issuers with zero shareholders
Foreign private issuers with no U.S. holders ever without exception

It holds only real estate for personal use with no investors

prompt: Rule 701 exempts employee equity compensation offerings if aggregate sales in 12 months do not exceed the greater of:

Unlimited amount with no disclosure ever
Only profits from the CEO's personal trading
$1 million, 15% of total assets, or 15% of outstanding securities measured by class

Only oral roadshow jokes that never appear in a filing
State property-tax assessments on issuer real estate
Failure to pay FINRA continuing-education fees

distractorExplanations.d: CE fees are an SRO obligation, not §11.

prompt: Exchange Act Section 13(d) requires beneficial ownership reporting on Schedule 13D within:

options.text: Ten years after any purchase
Five business days after crossing 5% beneficial ownership of a class of equity securities
Only if the issuer requests voluntarily
One hour before market open on any random day
